Access + team readiness

1 · Introduction

Series of videos, made by Dr. Stalbert, that will aid in our understanding of simplifying the process. Focusing on how to utilize the pipeline method to reach our end result of creating a game.

2 · Developer mindset

Video 1 - Game Developer Mindset - Overcoming the Obstacles \\Game Development, needing the proper mindset (open) - Creativity + Innovation. ---Maintaining a positive mindset and attitude to think inside and outside the box. ---Perseverance to keep eyes on the main goal, long journey ahead. -Uplifting one another through the storm, fostering teamwork + communication -Adaptability & Collaboration*** **Enjoying the Development Process Customer Focus (target audience) - |Key to Success| Needs of fans/users above everything *Changing the way you think* ---> Developing the Growth Mindset (A Process That Takes Time) \\Embrace challenges, seek out the uncomfortable situations ---Learn from failures, don't be discouraged, analyze them and move forward (grow) ---Focus on Effort : Hard work + Dedication ---Be able to receive feedback/constructive criticism ---Surround yourself w/ positive role models (inspire and new growth/knowledge) **Keep Learning** - Key to developing that growth mindset >Don't be afraid to try new things \\Practice as to refine new and old skills >Technical Challenges - bugs, hardware issues, code structure \\Strong team with diverse technical skills + testing protocol ---Record keeping to aid in troubleshooting when stuck >Scope Creep: Don't get carried away with features and new ideas. Stick to the idea and what makes sense within the story. \\\Need a clear vision from the beginning and proper communication b/w the team ---Marketing and Distribution ---->Knowing the Target Audience<----- >Funding >Burnout & Mental Health \__Taking a step away, balancing work and regular life Community helps ground the nerves and therefore the person >Stay Motivated by setting clear goals/task lists w/ deadlines \\Small and manageable tasks build large components ---Celebrate small wins along the way (keeping morals high) ---Taking small/appropriate breaks >Staying Organized \\Keep track of tasks, deadlines, records \___Game Development Document to keep the team in line with the goal and on the same page >Maintain The Passion \Supposed to be a fun process >Collaborate and Communicate x3 \B/w all members of the development team, from "smallest" members to "largest" \\Proper check-ins

02 · My contribution

My understanding of the job

Well the finish line is a completed game containing a story and certain components that are beloved by the team of creators. >As for the work, it is a lengthy process. -First, attaining the proper mindset to grow and develop. -Other more logistical components are to keep a master document that can be referenced by all of the team so everyone is in line with the project and its deadlines/tasks. Proper file storage and record keeping. -It will take facing challenges and overcoming them, learning from failure, to push through to the other side. -The coding part can be delegated to others, including AI. The truly difficult part is creating a story in which you are the #1 fan.

What I will contribute

My contributions to a team, at first glance, are more conceptual and connective. -Others are more skilled with the technology, but I believe my ideas are sharp and quite helpful in the overall collaboration and story building. In the previous class, I was the main transcriber on the whiteboard of all the brainstorming we did. Anyone can work with the tech: that can be delegated like I have said. But being able to do the physical world things with a team is what make me valuable to a team. Keeping us in line and in the scope of where our story lies. Uplifting others to share ideas, whether they are appropriate in that moment or not. Team collaboration and proper communication to straighten our path to discovering the story within.

Where I need support

As mentioned, the technical aspects can be improved. I am familiar with AI usage, but in regards to getting it to code for me, my knowledge is fairly rudimentary. Aside from that, attaining that growth and developer mindset is still needing improvement. Facing the challenges, learning from mistakes, getting comfortable with being uncomfortable.

03 · Huddle + plan

Team / solo mission

DUFF

David Lopez · lead / Jesse Sanchez

Story + playable goal

A 2-D wave-based game with escalating difficulty as the rounds progress. Online/offline, up to 4 players total. The main goal is to see how far you can get until the enemies overwhelm you and defeat you.

Our decision framework

P2P can be advantageous in the development by guiding us to the end point of where our team wants the game to stand. There is not much of a story to derive from this type of game, as opposed to other single-player, story mode games, but an underlying story to the characters can help immersify the fans.

Production pipeline

Unnamed stage story inputs/assets build + configure output/scene test+handoff · owner Jesse · 2026-11-12T12:46 to 2026-11-12T13:46 Pacific Pipeline to get the story to become a reality. Design and being creative with the characters, story, enemies, and weapons should be a main focus.

Engine, assets + technology

Definitely will be using Unity, and even moreso a 2-D template as the foundation. C# with all its variables and functions.

Future reuse + credits

The whiteboard, storyboarding process can be a concept that is easily transferable across projects and different stories. Understanding every element of the story is what builds and drives the foundation. It guides where the story will and should end.

Huddle decisions + open questions

Black Ops Zombies arcade was the main inspiration for the game. Different enemies, characters, stories and whatnot, but a 2-d wave-based game that increasing in difficulty. The remaining questions revolve around ui and design; what the enemies and characters may look like
